niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong, readable hierarchy; rounded, card-based components; and layouts that feel organized and intentionally grouped. They frequently like light, airy, neutral surfaces with soft contrast, but also sometimes prefer dark premium themes when paired with clear contrast and focused emphasis. Across contexts, they consistently respond well to cleaner structure, prominent primary actions, restrained visual noise, and polished card/modal presentations rather than flat, scattered, or weakly grouped layouts.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers clear hierarchy with strong titles, obvious section separation, grouped metadata, dividers/cards, and one primary focal area rather than flat or weakly separated layouts.
Prefers rounded cards, pill-shaped controls, modal/card framing, soft container treatment, and integrated grouped surfaces over square, border-heavy, or directly-on-background layouts.
Generally prefers layouts with breathing room, generous padding, and fewer competing elements, though in some utility/list contexts they also accept denser information if it improves scan efficiency.

Shows a mixed but strong pattern around color treatment: often prefers light neutral backgrounds with dark text and soft contrast, but also likes dark premium themes when contrast is clear and the palette feels polished rather than muddy or overly saturated.

Often prefers simplified, focused content with fewer competing metrics or explanatory elements, but in practical browsing/selection screens also values efficient information visibility and richer detail when it supports decision-making.

Prefers clear, prominent actions such as full-width or visually dominant buttons, highlighted primary CTAs, and secondary actions that are still visibly contained rather than text-only or weakly emphasized.

Prefers content organized into clear cards, rows, labeled sections, or consolidated groups with explicit structure rather than scattered elements, mixed panels, or undifferentiated continuous layouts.
